As of August 2014, we are also responsible for ensuring that the people of Ireland are protected from the harmful effects of radiation. The EPA is an independent public body established under the Environmental Protection Agency Act, 1992. The other main instruments from which we derive our mandate are the Waste Management Act, 1996, and the Protection of the Environment Act, 2003 and Radiological Protection (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 2014. We have a wide range of functions to protect the environment, and our primary responsibilities include: Environmental licensing Enforcement of environmental law Environmental planning, education and guidance Monitoring, analysing and reporting on the environment Regulating Ireland's greenhouse gas emissions Environmental research development Strategic environmental assessment Waste management Radiological protection Further information is available at our corporate website www.epa.ie. Objectives of this tender The Assisted Human Reproduction Regulatory Authority (AHRRA) is seeking a partner for the provision of website design and development, and support services for this website and other websites under the authority’s remit. Website design and development is required for a public facing website that will contain separate elements for Industry users and the general public. Support services (i.e. hosting, maintenance) are required for this website. AHRRA Website The AHRRA website will comprise a fundamental component of our digital communications strategy and is essential in our communications with our stakeholders. The primary purpose of the AHRRA website will be to build the AHRRA’s presence as a new Regulatory Authority so that we can inform and increase the knowledge of prospective and existing stakeholders on the role and function of the AHRRA. A key function of the website will be providing assistance to stakeholders, potential licensees and the public on how they can effectively engage with the authority through the provision of guid

to be easily understood and accessible. For AHR Treatment Providers The AHRRAs website will comprise a fundamental component of our digital communications strategy and is essential in our communications with AHR treatment providers, those working in the AHR industry and potential license applicants (licensees). There will also be legal personnel who support families in securing parental orders for children born through donor-assisted human reproduction and surrogacy arrangements. The primary purpose of the AHRRA website for AHR Treatment Providers will be to inform and increase the knowledge of prospective and existing licensees requiring licensing services of the AHRRA so that they may benefit to the maximum extent from their engagement with the authority. The ‘AHR treatment provider’ sections of the website will follow the ‘public facing’ pages in style, layout and navigation but will be aimed at providing access to technical specifications, guides and documentation as well as providing direct links to both AHRRA and 3rd party web applications. be available to the public via the website. The underpinning technology will not be agreed for some time. It is expected that the various registers will operate in a predefined ‘frame’ within the main AHRRA website with navigation and search functionality provided by the relevant ICT provider. It should not be apparent to a website visitor that the content from the various AHRRA registers are coming from an alternative source. Examples of similar embedded registers can be found on the websites of the Teaching Council (www.teachingcouncil.ie) and the Charities Regulator (www.charitiesregulator.ie). It is envisaged that applications for licensing, surrogacy agreements and for donor-assisted AHR arrangements will open the application system in a new browser window that is not integrated with the main AHRRA website. deliverables_scope.text: his procurement This procurement establishes a single-supplier framework agreement and awards the first call-off under it through one open competition. The terms below govern the framework. Nature and term The framework is a single-supplier arrangement for a term of one year from the date of award with an option to extend for two further one-year periods (up to a combined three years). For the avoidance of doubt, it should be stated that the period for delivery of any subsequent contracts entered into under the framework may extend beyond the date of expiry of the framework. It does not commit Dublin Rape Crisis Centre to any minimum volume or value of work beyond the first call- off. It establishes the supplier, the scope, the terms and the pricing against which Dublin Rape Crisis Centre may place further call-offs at its discretion during the term. Scope The framework covers the creative design and production of Dublin Rape Crisis Centre's flagship public-awareness and behaviour-change advertising campaigns. This includes, but is not limited to, the Signs of Hope campaign and any successor flagship campaign that replaces or develops it. Media buying is procured separately and Dublin Rape Crisis Centre shall be under no obligation to purchase a minimum amount of service

tisfactory performance and any required approval. There is no guarantee that any future call-off will be placed. Placing a call-off At the discretion of the buyer, future call-offs are awarded directly to the supplier under the framework terms, within the agreed scope, ceiling and rate card. Where a future brief requires detail not fixed by this tender, Dublin Rape Crisis Centre may consult the supplier in writing to supplement their tender before the call-off is placed. No new advertised competition is required for a call-off that falls within scope. The buyer reserves the right to call a new competition at any point. First call-off specification: Signs of Hope, Wave 3 Context for the campaign Sexual violence is at epidemic levels in Irish society. As the CSO has revealed, more than half of women and almost a third of men have experienced sexual violence in their lifetimes, so the need for our services is enormous. However, the same CSO survey shows that only about one in five of those affected will consult a support service. Reasons for this lack of engagement include general victim-blaming attitudes, self-blame and shame. Many others are simply not aware of the supports Dublin Rape Crisis Centre | Request for Tender Page 4 available, or believe that the supports are not

alised, non-judgmental support is there for them 24/7, for free and in confidence; • Survivors of all forms of sexual violence – not only rape – can seek support. This includes online abuse, street harassment and workplace sexual harassment; • They are not alone – support is available; and • Others have walked this path before them and healing is possible. Targets • Increase in calls to the National Rape Crisis Helpline during the campaign, particularly from lesser-heard groups. • Wider recognition and awareness of the National Helpline and our wider supports. • Increased national and local media coverage and social media traction. Scope of work for the first call-off • Assessment of the current body of creative assets from the 2024 and 2025 campaigns, towards a potential refresh or change in direction. • Creative design and delivery of a national campaign. • Liaison with the media buying agency and with the Dublin Rape Crisis Centre team as required. Timeline In 2024 and 2025 we launched and ran the campaign over Q4. In 2026 we envisage a longer-term approach, closer to an always-on campaign delivered in bursts across the year, starting as soon as possible but no later than October 2026. before the original deadline date. Dublin Rape Crisis Centre is funded through a mixture of state support, primarily through the Cuan agency, and other sources such as philanthropic and corporate donors and public donations. Organisational priorities Goal 1. High quality protection, through timely services and supports focused on supporting recovery, building resilience and attaining justice for those harmed by rape and other forms of sexual violence. Goal 2. Effective prevention, informed by the lived experiences of victims and survivors of sexual violence (through advocacy, education, and legal, policy and research work). Goal 3. A sustainable organisation, which effectively manages risk and proactively supports its people towards excellence in meeting the needs of victims/survivors.
